Targeted re-review (round 3) — sprint `2026-09-20-evidence-pipeline-integrity`, review_run_id 0ce0071a-2a2d-4d40-8218-384031e02fde, mode: design. Read-only; no files written. Hashes re-verified on disk: design.md = 1c92e00c…6a88, review-packet.md = 07e7f7fe…7db11 (both match dispatch); packet `source_design_sha256` matches design.md.

Round-2 P1s:
- `&` operator vs. guard: CLOSED — the guard is out of the write set (design.md:27,121, packet "Allowed write set" line 37), so the "adding `&` changes live guard decisions" contradiction is structurally gone; `echo hi & rm -rf /` keeps tokenizing as one segment under the untouched `pre-bash-guard.cjs:140-143` / `pre-bash-guard.py:182-185`. The `&` rule now lives only in `_shell-lex` and is redirection-aware (design.md:39-40), which also protects AC1's own `npm test 2>&1 | tail -8`. Baseline verified: `git diff --stat 52ff57eb -- <three guard paths>` is empty, so the "before" side of AC5 is a well-defined, checkable commit.
- CX quote-blindness: CLOSED — `_shell_lex.py` is written fresh (design.md:27,31,111) instead of extracting `split_segments` (`pre-bash-guard.py:176-188`), so the CX splitter that turned `go test -run 'A|B' ./...` into two fragments is never in the evidence path. CC/CX verdict parity for the quoted-pipe rows is now reachable.
- `&&` rule: CLOSED and correct — design.md:51,56. Under condition 2, `npm test && echo ok` and both segments of `npm run lint && npm test` are provable, which matches bash left-operand propagation. The round-2 contradiction is resolved explicitly at design.md:56.
- Per-segment re-classification: CLOSED — design.md:46 names the step and the reason it works. Verified: `COMMAND_PREFIX` at `_input-binding.cjs:8` and `_input_binding.py:18`, both compiled with `m`/`re.M`, so an isolated segment matches on the `^` alternative. `npm test 2>&1` and `npm run lint` both classify standalone.

Matrix: OK — all 14 rows of the Provable column follow from the three-condition rule as written; no row contradicts it. Spot-derivations: `npm run lint && npm test` — `lint` segment passes cond1, cond2, cond3; `test` segment trivially; "yes" correct. `set -o pipefail; npm test 2>&1 | tail -8` — the redirection rule keeps `2>&1` inside the segment, segment re-classifies as `test`, cond1 via pipefail, cond2 vacuous because V's pipeline is the last pipeline, and the leading `;` sits before V so it never enters cond2; "yes" correct. `npm test &` — not provable. `go test -run 'A|B' ./...` — quote-aware scan yields one segment, classifies `test` at `^`, no operators; "yes" correct.
  The one real gap is in the Reason column, not the verdict: two rows fail more than one condition and the design never pins reason precedence. `npm test | tail -8 || echo done` fails cond1 and cond2; `npm test &` fails cond2 and cond3. The table is self-consistent under exactly one precedence — 3 then 2 then 1, the reverse of the order the conditions are listed at design.md:50-52. An implementer evaluating in the listed order and returning the first failure gets the wrong reason for both rows. Self-correcting because the table is the test matrix, so P2, but it should be one sentence since AC3 demands reason equality across two independent implementations.

[P1] design.md:95 — the fail-open analysis cites the right two facts but reaches the wrong conclusion, because it only considers the guard consumer; requiring `_shell-lex` at `_input-binding` module load puts the delivery gate on the new module's load path, and the gate fails open on all three platforms — The two cited facts check out: `pre-bash-guard.cjs:356-358` wraps the `_input-binding` require in its own try/catch that writes stderr and does not set `process.exitCode`, and it runs after the guard's blocking analysis, so a load failure there really does cost only evidence capture; `athena-gates.ts:42-43` really does map any non-2 exit to allow. But `_input-binding` has three more consumers that require it at module top level with no try: `delivery-gate.cjs:15`, `evidence-collector.cjs:7`, `_review-binding.cjs:4`, mirrored at `cc-core/delivery-gate.cjs:15` and `cc-core/_review-binding.cjs:4`, and on CX at `delivery-gate.py:28`. A missing or broken `_shell-lex`/`_shell_lex` therefore throws at gate import time, before any of the gate's fail-closed logic runs — CC treats exit 1 as non-blocking, Pi returns null from `blockDecision`, CX produces no block JSON. The gate's own contract (fail-closed at ship, `delivery-gate.py:12-14`) is bypassed at import. So the design's claim that this placement preserves today's degradation shape is false: today's shape is "evidence capture degrades, guard and gate survive"; the proposed shape is "ship gate silently allows".
  This is not merely more surface on an existing chain. The existing integrity check does not cover the new file: `REQUIRED_ASSETS` at `setup-athena.py:136-148` lists `_input-binding.cjs` / `_input_binding.py` but cannot list the new module, and `managed_complete` (:152-153) would report a home missing it as complete, so the repair path never fires. The File Structure Plan does not include `setup-athena.py`, and Non-goal design.md:126 reads as "do not touch the installer". Mitigating facts: `source_files` at `setup-athena.py:207-227` rglobs `hooks/`, so a fresh install does carry the new file, and AC5's Pi parity list already names `_shell-lex.cjs`. Minimal close: either (a) require `_shell-lex` lazily inside `validationStatusPolicy` so only the collector path depends on it, and state that a load failure yields a non-provable result (fail-closed for evidence, gate untouched), or (b) keep module-load require and add the new module to `REQUIRED_ASSETS` plus `setup-athena.py` to the file plan. (a) is strictly safer and costs one line.

[P2] design.md:50-52 vs. matrix rows `npm test | tail -8 || echo done` and `npm test &` — reason precedence is unstated and the only self-consistent order is the reverse of the listed one — pin "evaluate 3 then 2 then 1, report the first failure". Without it, two independent implementations satisfying AC3's reason-equality clause can still disagree on untested multi-failure inputs such as `npm test | tail -8 &`.

[P2] design.md:37,42 + condition 2 wording — "end of line" is used to mean "end of the command string", but newline is in the control-operator list — the safe reading is already the natural one, but CC's Bash tool routinely carries multi-line commands, and a literal per-line reading would make `npm test` on line 1 provable while the observed exit 0 comes from line 2, a false pass. One clause ("the whole command string is one line for this rule; newline behaves as `;`") removes the only reading that produces a wrong PASS.

[P2] design.md:46,56 — the zero-classified-segment case is unspecified — `classifyValidation` is quote-blind, so `echo "x; npm test"` classifies as `test` on the whole string today and gets a pre-hook snapshot, while the policy re-classifies per quote-aware segment. I could not construct a case where the whole string classifies and no segment does, so this is not a correctness hazard — but "every one must satisfy all three conditions" is vacuously true over an empty set, and the design should say the vacuous case keeps today's `pass`.

[P2] design.md:54 — the `set` scan is unconditional — `false && set -o pipefail; npm test | tail -8` would be scored as pipefail-enabled and admitted, a false PASS direction. Contrived enough to be acceptable, but it is the one place the `set` rule is unsound rather than merely conservative; a line in Non-goals would close it.

On the two remaining questions that did not produce findings:
- Two scanners in the tree is not a correctness hazard now. The guard's segmenter and `_shell-lex` answer disjoint questions over the same string, the guard is byte-frozen by AC5, and the pre-hook capture path is unchanged (design.md:81), so divergence cannot flip a guard decision and cannot realistically flip a classification. The scheduled-debt owner is named (slice 8, design.md:30,120). Style-only from here.
- AC5 is provable as stated. The "before" side is pinned by `base_commit: 52ff57eb…` and checkable with `git diff --exit-code 52ff57eb -- <the three guard paths>`; all three paths are tracked and currently unchanged from that commit. The Pi parity side is satisfiable today: `cc-core/_input-binding.cjs` = CC `_input-binding.cjs` (30a88e4bf884800b…) and `cc-core/pre-bash-guard.cjs` = CC `pre-bash-guard.cjs` (3a9ee518d015c883…); `_shell-lex.cjs` exists on neither side, so the three-file list is complete and correct. Only suggestion (P2): AC5's before/after clause names no mechanism while its parity clause says "asserted by test"; naming the `git diff --exit-code` command makes it runnable at review. Real-chain AC1/AC4 are feasible — `test_state_review.py` already builds temp git repos and pipes payloads into hooks.

AC bijection: OK — design.md yields 6 criteria to {AC1…AC6}; review-packet.md yields {AC1…AC6}; missing = empty, extra = empty. Packet is 37 lines against the 80-line limit; design.md is 127 lines against the System 200 warning threshold; `source_design_sha256` matches design.md on disk. Every AC is falsifiable, including AC5, whose round-2 unobservability is fixed by the byte-identity formulation plus the new test mandate at design.md:114.

VERDICT: CONCERNS
